structured_output.what_is_happening: A token named "Pokémon" was deployed straight to a PumpSwap pool. The pool appeared 2 seconds after the mint and migrated_unix is 0, so it never went through a pump.fun bonding curve. The creator supplied the liquidity, and that LP is 0% locked and 0% burned. In about 44 minutes it traded roughly $373k of volume against a $58k market cap (5.4x turnover), rose about 168%, and drew about 1,113 unique buyers. Buy and sell counts are now almost even (m5: 241 buys vs 228 sells). The pool holds 57.5% of supply. One wallet that GMGN tags as dev/team holds 10.55%, and the creator's own wallet shows zero balance. At least 9 other "Pokémon" tokens exist from the past few days. Nearly all have liquidity of $0 to $0.37, including one showing a $1.4M market cap with $0.01 liquidity. That looks like a series of identical launches that were rugged.

narrative.description: This is a generic mega-IP name, Pokémon, with no website, socials, description or DexScreener profile. Nothing in the packet points to a specific catalyst. The name is a recycled ticker that has been launched over and over in recent days.
narrative.why_spreading: The attention probably comes from a famous-name ticker plus a fast chart on PumpSwap drawing in bots and degens. The same name has been launched repeatedly, so there may be some off-packet Pokémon news (a game or card release), but the packet has no evidence of one.

token_connection.why_this_token: It is currently the only live 'Pokémon' pair with real liquidity and volume. That comes from timing, not from any claim to be the canonical token.
token_connection.competing_tokens: At least 9 same-name tokens, almost all with near-zero liquidity. One (8jwv...) shows a $1.4M mcap with $0.01 liquidity, and another (HqfY...) created about 8 minutes earlier had $53k h1 volume and now has $0 liquidity. That points to rapid launch-and-pull cycles on this name.

authenticity.evidence: Holder spread looks fairly broad: 1,113 unique buyers, top 10 holders excluding the pool at 14%, a bot/degen rate of 0, and 0 fresh wallets. There is no paid promotion and no smart or KOL wallets. Against that: 6 bundler wallets, a 10.55% dev/team holding, creator-supplied unlocked LP, and a string of same-name rugs. GeckoTerminal shows only 107 unique sellers against 1,113 buyers, possibly because of window caps, while sell transactions nearly match buys. That suggests a small number of wallets doing heavy selling.
authenticity.uncertainty: There is no X or Telegram data, so I can't tell whether real Pokémon-related news is driving it. GMGN's zero bot rate is inconsistent with the size of the transaction counts.

structural_risks: The creator deployed straight to PumpSwap with their own LP, which is 0% locked or burned, so they can pull it at any moment

structured_output.counterargument: Unlike most pulled clones, this pool shows real breadth: more than 1,100 buyers, low holder concentration outside the pool, and deep liquidity ($69k) relative to market cap. Also, whoever supplied the LP might keep it in place to collect fees rather than pull it.

structured_output.thesis: This is a generic mega-IP ticker deployed straight to PumpSwap with creator-controlled, unlocked LP and a 10.55% team holding. It sits next to a string of same-name tokens whose liquidity is now $0. That setup most likely ends with the liquidity pulled. The buyer breadth is real enough to allow a brief further pump, but the expected value of the 2x/-50% bracket entered 25 minutes after detection is poor.
